claim: /lio/health has two producers on two threads with different stamp bases and different semantics: the scan path (fast_lio_main) stamps with scan end time and sets correction_fresh=hasCorrectedOutput(); the propagated path (lio_propagated, 50 Hz) stamps with the latest propagated IMU time (always later than the last scan end) and sets correction_fresh by age. The PX4 adapter drops any health whose stamp is <= the last accepted one (navigation_mode_node.cpp:1625-1627), so every scan-path message, including the DEGRADED/LOST failure edge, is discarded. Because the propagated worker stops publishing as soon as the main estimator is invalid, the adapter keeps the last healthy propagated assessment and only fails closed by the 0.2 s staleness lease. propagation_valid_ is also latched true by every propagated publish (line 713) and cleared only by the 1 Hz transport timer (line 889-892), so it carries no information in any accepted message.
failure_scenario: Tracking, t_scan_end=10.0 s; propagated health already published at 10.04. Scan 10.1 fails registration -> pipeline Degraded -> scan-path health DEGRADED stamped 10.1 arrives after propagated health stamped 10.14 -> dropped. Worker invalidated -> no newer propagated health. Adapter's lio_health_valid_ stays true until state_stale_after_s (0.2 s) expires; evidence shows 'stale' instead of 'DEGRADED'.
direction: Give /lio/health one owner and one clock (e.g. a single health aggregator that publishes on state-change edges and at a fixed cadence, stamped with the propagated/output epoch), carry correction age instead of a per-path boolean, and derive propagation_valid from the worker's current status; add a producer-consumer ordering test for the failure edge.

claim: The patch path cannot win for the product sensor. The dirty region is the AABB of the ray origin and every (clipped) endpoint. For a 360-degree LiDAR with a 50x50x8 m update box this AABB covers almost the whole window, so the estimate exceeds 0.4 of full and falls back to a full export. Every map slide (threshold 1.5 m) also forces a full export. Each full export walks and copies 251x251x41 base cells plus the inflated grid and allocates about 6.8 MB per publication (20 Hz period).
failure_scenario: Evidence runtime_evidence/2026-09-04/E05_single_hot_replan_failure_cycle5/report.json records 296 full exports, 0 patches and world_snapshot_bytes 6840416. The export cost sits on the single mapping thread inside the 20 ms p50 / 57 ms max update, so the latest-only inbox drops scans at speed. The patch machinery (depth 8, change history) adds complexity without paying off.
direction: Make the dirty region a union of per-ray/voxel-chunk boxes (or a dirty-chunk bitmap) instead of one AABB; store snapshots as shared immutable chunks (copy-on-write per chunk) so publication cost scales with changed chunks; add a benchmark test.

claim: generateExpTraj is a ~1900-line function mixing hot-splice compatibility, guide sampling, A*, route-prefix certification, pass-through corner windows, terminal-velocity policy, SFC generation, speed governor and MINCO invocation; it mutates gi_.goal_p, planning_goal_p_, goal_endpoint_adjusted_, latest_guide_*, required/certified_lookahead_m_ as side effects mid-function.

claim: BACKUP braking seeds use terminal altitude = planning_goal_p_.z() when cfg_.preserve_backup_altitude, but planning_goal_p_ is overwritten earlier in generateExpTraj with the bounded local-prefix endpoint / lookahead endpoint (3358, 3931) or outgoing geometry goal (3234). claim: No tilt (attitude) constraint exists anywhere in the planning backend (no tilt field in Config/planner.yaml; grep finds none). Tilt is only implicitly limited by |a|<=max_acc and the thrust band. With the traj_opt boundary max_acc 12 m/s^2 (planner.yaml:98) horizontal acceleration alone implies ~51 deg tilt; the PX4 tilt limit is not an input of any certificate.
failure_scenario: A certified trajectory (e.g. backup/emergency using the 12 m/s^2 boundary, or a mission that does not lower the envelope) requires more tilt than PX4 allows; PX4 saturates attitude and the vehicle deviates from the corridor-certified path.
direction: Expose tilt from FlatnessMap::forward (z-axis) and certify it against an explicit, PX4-sourced tilt parameter as an Information need; add a test.

claim: Physical flatness parameters silently fall back to non-physical defaults (gravity 1.0 m/s^2, mass 1.0 kg, drag 0.7/0.8 vs product 0.35/0.35) when the key is missing; YamlLoader only printf's a warning (navigation_math/yaml_loader.hpp:75) and validate() accepts them. claim: Immediate-admission anchor check compares the candidate at activation_ns==now with the measured position stamped at state.source_stamp_ns (up to data_freshness_window 0.5 s older), i.e. a mixed-time error; runCycle computes the same concept time-aligned via sampleAtDeclaredStamp(execution_stamp_ns) (:5214-5222) and validateRetainedCommand keeps both raw and aligned errors (:7783-7791). For the emergency brake the check is tautological (the brake itself is started at now from the same stale state, see R3-09), so it can never detect a stamp offset; for stationary PlanFromRest it is harmless. The gate therefore certifies nothing about time alignment.
failure_scenario: Any immediate candidate whose start state is time-shifted relative to the measured lease (e.g. the emergency brake of R3-09, or a future moving immediate cutover) passes with anchor_error~0 because both sides use the same stale sample, while a correctly time-aligned candidate from a moving vehicle would be charged v*age of spurious error against the 0.75 m limit.
direction: Evaluate candidate at state.source_stamp_ns vs measured state (time-aligned) plus an explicit outer cap at now; one shared anchor-error helper for commit/runCycle/retained validation; unit test with aged lease.

claim: Execution-state freshness is decided by two different predicates for the same lease inside one admission: commitPlannerCandidate uses ROS-time-only classifyTimestampFreshness (also runCycle :4369-4370, :5504-5505), while admitImmediateCandidate (:2922-2925), tickMissionProgress (:2739-2741), goal activation (:2442-2445) and the mapping endpoint path (:1069-1075) use evaluateExecutionStateFreshness which additionally bounds steady-clock receive age.

direction: Unify on one typed freshness predicate (ROS source + steady receive) owned by navigation_execution and use it at every runtime gate; add test for fresh-source/stale-receive lease.

claim: The executor has only 2 threads (navigation_runtime_main.cpp:6) and propagated odometry is in a Reentrant group; every ingress callback (odom, scan, health) takes localization_epoch_ingress_mutex_ and odometry holds it plus localization_transition_mutex_ for its whole body. During resetForLocalizationEpochLocked the ingress lock is held across the mapping drain (:1966-1970). A second odometry message dispatched on the other thread blocks on the same ingress mutex, leaving zero threads for the 50 Hz command timer and the mission timer.
failure_scenario: Localization epoch bump while a raycast update is in flight (tens-hundreds of ms): both executor threads parked on ingress; publishCommand stops -> adapter command-stream timeout/handover instead of an orderly hold; mission/progress timers stall.
direction: Give the command timer a dedicated executor thread or node; make odometry MutuallyExclusive; move the drain off the ingress path; add a starvation test with a slow mapping drain.

claim: Every 50 Hz command tick deep-copies two NavigationGoal messages (each carrying the full RouteSnapshot arrays and strings) while holding localization+input+transition locks, and then, for PASS_THROUGH MAIN samples, calls certifiedMainContinuationWindow (:9369-9375) which runs decodeRouteSnapshot (:337, :208-324: builds Mission, RouteProgress, segment and arc vectors); on traj_finish it decodes the route again (:9218-9219). Heap allocation and O(waypoints) work on the real-time path, part of it under the global locks.
failure_scenario: Long missions (up to kMaximumMissionWaypoints) make every command tick allocate and copy the whole route; lock hold time of the command transaction grows with mission size and delays odometry/mapping/planner transactions; allocator jitter shows up as command period jitter.
direction: Share immutable goal/route via shared_ptr<const> captured by pointer under the lock; decode the route once at goal admission and store the ImmutableRouteSnapshot in the execution record; add a command-tick allocation benchmark.

claim: The ROS publish of the NavigationCommand (publish_ros_command -> command_publisher_->publish, reliable QoS) and rememberMissionCommandIssued (copy of the full command into a deque) execute inside the publishIfCurrent callback (:9676-9677) while localization_transition_mutex_, input_mutex_, the command transition mutex and the ExecutionAuthority publish lock are all held. Middleware serialization/transport therefore extends the global critical section that the mapping publication finalizer (:1237-1291), odometry ingress (:2101-2160) and every planner transaction also need.
failure_scenario: A slow DDS write (reliable QoS, discovery burst, loaded SITL host) stalls odometry ingestion and the mapping world publication for the same duration; the next command tick then sees a superseded lease or aged state (see R3-15) and the stall propagates into freshness failures.
direction: Linearize exposure by recording an immutable 'authorized command' token under the lock and perform the transport publish outside all lifecycle locks (the adapter already validates lease/identity); measure last_publish_us under load.

claim: publishCommand loads the lease L1 (:8888) before taking the lifecycle locks and silently returns without publishing when a newer lease L2 was published while it waited. onPropagatedOdometry holds localization_transition_mutex_ across execution_state_store_.publish (:2101-2160), so a command tick that coincides with an odometry callback is dropped by construction, and any lock hold longer than one odometry period guarantees a drop. No counter or log records these skips.
failure_scenario: Planner/mapping transaction holds the locks for >1 odometry period at each of several consecutive ticks (e.g. during goal handoff or world recertification) -> several consecutive silent tick drops; command valid_until is now+100 ms, so the adapter sees the stream lapse and hands over although a certified command existed.
direction: Re-load the lease under the lock and evaluate it (the final exposure block already does this at :9586) instead of returning; count skipped ticks in diagnostics; test with high-rate odometry and injected lock hold.

excerpt: // The worker interrupt is deliberately post-action: cancelActive() may ⏎ // enter backend code and must not run while lifecycle locks are held.
claim: The stated rule is violated at many sites that call planning_worker_->cancelActive() with lifecycle locks held: :1907 (ingress+localization), :2361 (input+transition via onGoal/applyValidatedGoalLocked), :2628 (localization+input+transition), :4557 and :4745 (runCycle, all three), :9275 cancelActiveIfExecutionIdentity (all three). cancelActive holds the worker mutex and calls Planner::cancelActiveSolve, which locks Planner::solve_commit_mutex_ (planner.hpp:603-606); that mutex is also held while the heading-rebind export is constructed (planner.cpp:1673-1690) and during commit authorization (planner.cpp:823). cancelActiveSolve is not noexcept yet is called from noexcept cancelActive.
failure_scenario: Heading worker is inside its export under solve_commit_mutex_ when a terminal ModeStatus arrives: onModeStatus blocks in cancelActive while holding all three lifecycle locks; the 50 Hz command timer and odometry callbacks queue behind it for the duration of backend work.
direction: Make cancellation a lock-free atomic stop request (no backend mutex), document one lock order including worker/planner mutexes, and move cancel calls after lock release consistently; add a lock-order checker test.

claim: PlanningWorker claims sole ownership of the mutable planner (also :175-176 'callers cannot run arbitrary backend operations'), but NavigationRuntimeNode keeps a raw planner_ alias (navigation_runtime_node.hpp:636, cpp:1684) and invokes the facade from three other threads without backend_access_mutex_: command timer (commitPlannerCandidate/discardCommandCandidate/discardRetainedPositionHeadingCandidate via consumeHeadingRebind :8620), planning timer (committedSnapshot :3836) and HeadingRebindWorker (buildImmediateHeadingRebindCandidate :3869). direction: Remove the raw alias; route every facade call through PlanningWorker (or a typed read-only snapshot interface + an explicit heading-slot API with owner tokens).

excerpt: # remaining 0.02 s of the 0.08 s solve deadline is reserved for corridor, ⏎ total_time_limit_s: 0.06
claim: Two budget statements in the same product config disagree: A* may consume total_time_limit_s=0.06 of solve_deadline_s=0.08, leaving 0.02 s 'for corridor, MINCO, yaw, backup construction and final certification' (:200-203), while finalization_reserve_s=0.04 (:45-48) reserves 0.04 s just for the yaw+BACKUP finalization. 0.06 + 0.04 > 0.08.
failure_scenario: A solve where A* uses its full stage budget (new obstacle, fallback attempt) enters corridor/MINCO with less time than the finalization reserve, so nominal refinement is skipped/negative and the bundle misses its deadline (kNoCompleteBundleAtDeadline) exactly in the obstacle-reveal case the A* retry exists for.
direction: Express the solve budget as one typed partition validated at startup (sum of stage budgets + reserve <= deadline) instead of comments; add a config validation test.

claim: On an IMU gap the synchronizer sets its epoch to gap_end. Because the gap search runs up to end_bracket (first IMU >= scan end), gap_end can lie after the rejected scan's end, so the next contiguous scan (start == previous end < gap_end) is rejected as OVERLAPPING_LIDAR_INTERVAL. One IMU gap therefore costs two scans, the second one mislabelled as a LiDAR overlap, and each counts toward lifecycle.lost_after_registration_failures via recordUncorrectedUpdate.
failure_scenario: Reproduced (out/R4/repro/gap_overlap.cpp): IMU 5 ms spacing with a 1195->1230 ms hole, scans [1100,1200],[1200,1300] -> scan1 discontinuity gap_end=1230, scan2 'ERROR OVERLAPPING_LIDAR_INTERVAL ... overlap_duration_ns=30000000'. Evidence/diagnostics blame LiDAR timing (overlap_rejected_count) for an IMU transport gap; lost counter advances twice.
direction: Classify scans that start before a discontinuity resume time as 'SKIPPED_BY_IMU_DISCONTINUITY' (distinct status code and counter), or trim/propagate that scan from resume_time; add a test for a gap straddling a scan boundary.

claim: IMU-discontinuity recovery (and the forward-mismatch rebase at lines 489-490) is a zero-order hold: position/velocity/attitude from the last committed state time are relabelled with the later resume time without any propagation, and the valid IMU samples between state_time_ and gap_begin are erased by the synchronizer. The pose at resume_time is wrong by roughly v*(resume_time - state_time_) (scan period + gap), which the next ICP must absorb from an inflated covariance.
failure_scenario: Tracking at 5 m/s, 100 ms scans, a 35 ms IMU hole just before a scan end: state held at t_prev while time jumps ~135 ms -> ~0.7 m position error baked into the prior of the next registration; status only goes Degraded, and the first correction after it produces a step in corrected odometry.
direction: Propagate the state up to gap_begin with the samples that exist (and constant-velocity/attitude-rate across the hole or mark position invalid), or keep the pre-gap samples in the buffer; add a unit test asserting position continuity v*dt across a short discontinuity.

claim: After every queued measurement (each IMU sample, 200+ Hz) the worker calls pipeline_.diagnostics(), which copies the whole EstimatorDiagnostics (many std::string fields) and runs fillStateDiagnostics, including a 23x23 SelfAdjointEigenSolver (fast_lio_pipeline.cpp:1616-1617) and a mutex, only to read the .processing sub-struct. publishAvailableResults() also runs processNext -> resetTransientDiagnostics per IMU sample.
failure_scenario: On the single fast_lio_main thread this per-IMU work competes with the scan-processing path; under load the queue shedding thresholds (fast_lio_node.cpp:312-316) trip earlier and the propagated worker is asked to shed load.
direction: Expose a cheap processingStatistics() accessor; compute covariance eigen diagnostics only in finalizeResult/per scan; add a micro-benchmark for the per-IMU path.

claim: Any core IMU rejection (a single duplicate/regressed stamp, clock-domain mismatch, buffer full) forces the propagated worker to kDegraded/navigation_valid=false with correction_sequence 0. Nothing restores it until the next ProcessResult (next scan, ~100 ms), so an isolated duplicate IMU stamp blanks propagated odometry for a scan period even though the main estimator is still Tracking; the status the worker sees disagrees with the pipeline's own status_.
failure_scenario: Gazebo publishes two IMU messages with identical stamp (allow_equal_timestamps=false in measurement_buffer.cpp:13) -> kTimestampRegression -> worker Degraded -> downstream odometry bridge sees invalid propagated odometry for up to one scan period -> fail-closed hold.
direction: Send the pipeline's actual status after a rejection (or a typed 'ingress fault' flag distinct from estimator status) and restore it on the next accepted sample; count and threshold transient IMU rejections rather than latching on one.

claim: For every corrected scan, RosOutputPublisher::publish (called on the single fast_lio_main estimator thread) blocks up to kVisibilityAssociationWait=10 ms waiting for a matching visibility cloud, then converts up to 262144 points (makeFreeSpaceCloud) before the propagated worker receives the correction (fast_lio_node.cpp:784 precedes 796). IMU and the next scan wait behind it.
failure_scenario: Sim config sets input.visibility_points_topic; when the visibility cloud for a stamp is late or missing, each scan adds 10 ms to correction latency and to the propagated re-anchor delay; with 16-deep LiDAR queue and 0.2 s processing-lag gate this erodes headroom and delays the recovery edge.
direction: Move visibility association/free-space construction off the estimator thread (publisher/mapping-observation worker), enqueue the correction to the propagated worker before any output serialization, and measure it in RuntimeStatistics.

claim: A topic prior with any positive covariance entry becomes a 23x23 covariance whose unspecified blocks are Identity: extrinsic rotation 1 rad^2, extrinsic translation 1 m^2, gyro bias 1 (rad/s)^2, accel bias 1 (m/s^2)^2 (gravity is re-frozen by enforceFixedGravity). The pipeline applies it verbatim (fast_lio_pipeline.cpp:1366-1368). IkfomEstimator::initialize deliberately sets the extrinsic blocks to 1e-12 because the extrinsic is overwritten after each update (ikfom_estimator.cpp:373-378); with variance 1 the Kalman gain assigns part of every LiDAR correction to the extrinsic, which is then discarded, while P is shrunk as if the information was used.
failure_scenario: initial_prior.source=topic (not the current sim.yaml, which uses zero) with /px4/estimator_odometry covariance: first corrections under-correct pose and over-confident covariance; biases start at 1 (rad/s) std and can absorb gyro/accel errors.
direction: Build prior covariance through one typed function that starts from the estimator's own initial covariance (with frozen extrinsic/gravity blocks) and overrides only the mapped pose/velocity blocks; unit-test the resulting blocks.

With frames.odom != 'lio_odom', RosOdometrySerializer::serialize returns kFrameMismatch (ros_odometry_serializer.cpp:15-19) and both corrected and propagated publishers return silently, while /lio/health keeps publishing.
failure_scenario: A launch file renames frames.odom to 'odom': node starts, health reports TRACKING, but /lio/odometry_corrected, /lio/odometry_propagated, TF and mapping observations are never published; no error log.
direction: Either remove the frame parameters or inject the configured FrameIds into the core; validate the frame contract in the node path at startup (fail fast).

claim: The maximum usable IMU spacing exists as three independent values: timing.max_imu_gap_s (synchronizer, loaded from YAML, 0.02 in sim/dataset), ikfom.maximum_integration_step_ns (hard default 20 ms, never loaded by parameter_loader; it gates every IKFoM predict step and the propagated worker's continuity restart at imu_state_propagator.cpp:209-212), and buildPredictionImuSamples' configured_gap which is actually the group's *measured* max gap (fast_lio_pipeline.cpp:1041-1043). They agree today only because 0.02 s == 20 ms.

direction: Derive all three from one typed ImuContinuityPolicy loaded once from YAML; rename configured_gap to reflect that it is a measured value or compare against the configured limit; add a config-consistency test.

claim: ikd-tree maintenance (sort of all registered points, Add_Points with downsample=true for every point, and moving-cube Delete_Point_Boxes on 5 m motion) runs inline on fast_lio_main after each correction and before the result is published or the propagated worker re-anchors. There is no selective insertion (upstream FAST-LIO map_incremental skips points already represented in their voxel) and no time budget. This is the LIO-internal registration map, distinct from the planner mapping layer (N11).
failure_scenario: Crop events every 5 m at 5 m/s (1 Hz) plus full-scan downsampled insertion each scan add a periodic latency spike to correction publication; with the 0.5 s correction-age and 0.2 s processing-lag gates this is a candidate cause of periodic stale-correction stops.
direction: Publish the corrected result and hand the correction to the propagated worker before map maintenance; add selective insertion; measure p95/p99 of map_insert_crop_us in SITL and dataset before any change.

claim: publishTransportSnapshot (1 Hz wall timer) calls runtime_statistics_.populate() while holding input_mutex_ (fast_lio_node.cpp:834-840). populate() copies and sorts the full-run exact sample vector for 5 distributions x 3 percentiles (15 sorts), each growing by ~10 samples/s up to 65,536. input_mutex_ is taken by enqueue() for every IMU/LiDAR message and by fast_lio_main after every measurement, and the timer shares the single-threaded executor (main.cpp rclcpp::spin) with the IMU callback that feeds the propagated worker.
failure_scenario: After 30-60 min of flight each snapshot sorts ~20-36k elements 15 times under the ingress lock; IMU delivery to the propagated worker and the estimator loop stall for milliseconds once per second, growing with mission time, visible as periodic propagated-odometry jitter.
direction: Copy the raw counters under the lock and compute percentiles outside it, or keep a fixed-size streaming quantile/histogram; add a test bounding populate() time at 65,536 samples.

claim: All subscriptions and timers run on one single-threaded executor with the default callback group: PointCloud2/Livox conversion of up to 2,000,000 points (per-point bounds-checked memcpy in RosLidarAdapter::convert), visibility-cloud admission, the 0.5 s diagnostics snapshot, the 1 Hz transport snapshot (R4-19) and the IMU callback that fans IMU out to the propagated odometry worker. The propagated path's latency is therefore bounded by the longest of these callbacks, not by IMU rate.
failure_scenario: A large LiDAR message conversion (tens of ms) holds the executor; IMU samples queue in DDS and reach the propagated worker in a burst, so /lio/odometry_propagated publication timing jitters at LiDAR rate and consumers' freshness gates see gaps.
direction: Put the IMU subscription in its own mutually-exclusive callback group on a MultiThreadedExecutor (or a dedicated executor thread) and move point-cloud conversion off the IMU path; measure IMU callback latency distribution.

claim: LiDAR-blackout supervision (degraded_after 0.2 s, lost_after 1.0 s) is measured in host steady time, while every other estimator decision and all published stamps use the sensor/simulation clock domain. In SITL the two diverge by the Gazebo real-time factor; supervision runs only when the worker sees no input for 20 ms wall (fast_lio_node.cpp:603-610).
failure_scenario: Loaded CI host, Gazebo RTF ~0.2 with a 10 Hz sim LiDAR and ~250 Hz IMU: inter-scan wall gap ~0.5 s and IMU wall spacing ~20 ms -> LIDAR_TIMEOUT_DEGRADED_INERTIAL between every scan; each re-entry needs recovery_confirmation_updates=3 successes, so navigation_valid flaps (fail-closed storm) although no sim-time sample was missed. Conversely at RTF>1 a real sim-time blackout is detected late.
direction: Supervise LiDAR freshness in the estimator's clock domain (latest IMU time minus last LiDAR scan end) and keep wall-clock only for a separate process-liveness watchdog; test with a scaled-clock fixture.

claim: Hemisphere continuity is applied to the input NED quaternion, but the published ENU quaternion is rebuilt from a rotation matrix, whose sign is chosen by Eigen's trace/largest-diagonal branch; the continuity state is therefore ineffective and the output flips sign (repro_bridge_quat_sign.cpp: flip at NED yaw -149 deg, dot=-1.000).
failure_scenario: Vehicle yawing through ENU yaw about -120 deg: consecutive /px4/estimator_odometry (and /px4/sample_odometry_at_time interpolation inputs) jump q -> -q; any consumer that lerps/nlerps quaternions or compares components (not |dot|) sees a ~360 deg artificial rotation.
direction: Build the output quaternion as q_enu_flu = q(C_enu_ned) * q_ned_frd * q(C_flu_frd) (quaternion product) and apply the hemisphere check to the OUTPUT; add a yaw-sweep sign-continuity test.

claim: The probable-source-restart branch accepts the sample without the stale/future checks against now_ns that every other accepted sample must pass (lines 110-125).
failure_scenario: A delayed/replayed low-epoch sample (timestamp < 10 s) arriving after a long run is accepted as a restart: the bridge bumps frame_generation, clears history/reset compensation and publishes a sample whose age vs ROS now is unbounded.

failure_scenario: In-flight EKF2 yaw reset of 0.1 rad at 50 m from the startup origin: output position steps ~5 m while PX4 local position is continuous; evidence comparisons against PX4 then diverge.

claim: The authority's two most consequential mutators (activate pending -> active, revoke active) and all lifecycle helpers are declared const and work only because active_, staged_, lifecycle_, timeline_version_ and active_lineage_version_ are mutable. Any holder of a const ExecutionAuthority& (e.g. a read-only view passed to diagnostics/sampler code) can activate or revoke the command.

claim: Any non-off mode (including 'velocity-only' and 'adaptive') with the default zero base_m/alpha/beta silently sets suppress_braking AND suppress_estimator_health_response, disabling the adapter's tracking-envelope rejection for all roles and the fresh-unhealthy FAST-LIO fail-closed. external_mode.yaml states the opposite ('zero coefficients alone do not suppress safety responses').

claim: ProbMap returns BELOW_GROUND/ABOVE_CEILING before any mutation (no slide, no raycast), but MappingActor throws inside its try block. The catch(...) sets poisoned_=true, and MappingWorker::run marks the worker fatal (mapping_worker.hpp:224-240). A clean, non-mutating rejection is therefore treated as a partial commit.
failure_scenario: With virtual planes enabled in a non-lio_odom frame (the runtime only forbids lio_odom+planes, navigation_runtime_node.cpp:888-893), one pose sample below virtual_ground_height (for example z drift at rest) permanently stops mapping. Every later process() throws 'poisoned' and the mission fails closed.
direction: Split backend outcomes into rejected-before-mutation and mutated; return or throw a typed rejection without poisoning for the former; test a pose below the ground plane followed by a valid scan.

claim: InfMap copies Config before ProbMap re-quantizes the virtual plane heights, so two different plane heights coexist. With the production numbers (ceil 5.8, ground -1.1, res 0.2, step 4), ProbMap uses ceil 4.6 / ground -0.4 while InfMap uses 4.7 / -0.3. exportPlanningGrid derives inflated_virtual_* from the ProbMap copy, but live InfMap::getGridType uses its own copy. Config also floors 5.8/0.2=28.999... to 28 (config.hpp:575-577).
failure_scenario: If virtual planes are enabled, the snapshot's inflated plane boundary disagrees by 0.1 m with the live inflated map, and the evidence layer and inflated layer disagree on which z rows are walls. The planner and the parity tests see different ceilings. Latent: planner.yaml:233 disables the planes.
direction: Keep a single immutable post-quantization geometry object that ProbMap, InfMap and the export all read; compute plane indices with an integer/rounded conversion and add an export-vs-live test.

claim: local_map_origin_d_ = origin_i*res is a cell CORNER under ORIGIN_AT_CORNER, but cells span [(o-h)*r, (o+h+1)*r], so the true window centre is (o+0.5)*r. The exported local_center_m +/- local_size_m/2 box is therefore shifted by half a voxel (0.1 m) toward -xyz relative to the index bounds, and relative to the virtual_ground_m/virtual_ceiling_m exported in the same struct (which use the true faces).
failure_scenario: directionalSupportToLocalBoundary (world_model_view.hpp:135-) uses local_center_m/local_size_m. It over-reports support by 0.1 m toward the -x/-y/-z faces and under-reports it by 0.1 m toward +x/+y/+z, while contains()/classify use the index bounds. A route-support gate near the window edge therefore disagrees with classify by one half-cell.
direction: Derive local_center/size from global_min_index and dimensions (one source) or drop them from WorldGeometry; add a test that center+-size/2 equals the index-bound faces.

claim: The backend writes rog_map::GridType ordinals into base_state bytes, and the snapshot reinterprets them as navigation_world_model::CellState ordinals. The two enums only happen to share the order UNDEFINED,UNKNOWN,OUT_OF_MAP,OCCUPIED,KNOWN_FREE,FRONTIER (type_utils.hpp:43-50 vs world_model_view.hpp:24-31). No static_assert binds them, and the adapter (mapping_world_model_adapter.hpp:240-251) uses an explicit switch for the same mapping.
failure_scenario: If the upstream/vendored GridType is reordered (for example OCCUPIED<->KNOWN_FREE), snapshot validation still accepts the bytes (both are stored states), and every occupied voxel is published as KNOWN_FREE, which is an S1 outcome from a refactor, with no test catching it.
direction: Map with an explicit constexpr table/switch in exportPlanningGrid(+Region), or add static_asserts tying each GridType value to the CellState value.

claim: Every inflated-layer isSegmentTraversable ends with observedOccupiedTubeIsClear. That call scans every voxel of the segment's AABB grown by radius+1 cm (O(L^3), not O(L*r^2)), runs up to 8 patch lookups per voxel, and heap-allocates a PointVector per call.
failure_scenario: For a 20 m diagonal segment inside the 50x50x8 m window the AABB is about 66x66x40 = 174k voxels per query, and planners call this per candidate segment/goal check. This inflates solve time against the 0.08 s solve deadline (planner.yaml:44).
direction: Walk only voxels within the tube (DDA plus radius stencil), or use the inflated/ESDF layer for the coarse test and check centres only in the stencil; reuse a caller-owned buffer.

excerpt: printf("\033[0;33m Load param %s failed, use default value: \033[0;0m", param_name.c_str()); ⏎                 param_value = default_value;
claim: Config never passes required=true. Every mapping key, including evidence and safety semantics (raycasting/enable, ray_range, p_*, unk_thresh, virtual_ground_ceiling_en, map_sliding), silently falls back to a hard-coded upstream default when the key is missing or misspelt. Only a stdout line records the fallback. The production planner.yaml already relies on this for unk_inflation_en, unk_inflation_step, esdf and frontier keys.
failure_scenario: A typo such as 'ray_rang' makes ray_range default to [0.3, 10], cutting miss evidence to 10 m. Misspelling virtual_ground_ceiling_en re-enables absolute planes (default true) in lio_odom, which the runtime then rejects at startup only because it checks that flag explicitly. Other keys have no such guard.
direction: Mark every product-relevant key required (or load via a schema with explicit defaults listed in one table) and fail startup on unknown keys under rog_map/.

claim: Three hand-maintained profile->world alias maps (collision truth, simulator world, descriptor fallback) disagree: t2_same_identity_renewal maps to open in _collision_obstacles but long_open in _world_name_for_profile; long_three_pillars_multiwaypoint is missing from two of the three maps.
failure_scenario: If the registry lookup misses (renamed/removed registry entry, legacy CLI alias) the simulator launches long_open.sdf while the judge computes collision/clearance against open.sdf geometry -> wrong collision evidence. Currently masked because the registry entry wins first.
direction: Delete the alias dicts; resolve world exclusively from map_profiles.yaml (add explicit entries for smoke/open/speed/closed_loop_characterization) and fail on unknown profile.

claim: The default public scene (make run: MAP_SCENE=sanity_open TEST_CASE=positive) resolves to profile "open" (and fast -> "speed") which are not in the registry profiles; _scene_registry whitelists them via a hard-coded known_legacy set and _resolve_map_descriptor synthesizes a descriptor with expected_outcome hard-coded mission_complete, no mission field, no collision_truth, no benchmark.
failure_scenario: The canonical acceptance run bypasses the registry that is documented as the single source for geometry/mission/truth/expected outcome; its mission identity is resolved elsewhere and its descriptor cannot be audited against the registry.
direction: Register open/speed/smoke as first-class profiles in map_profiles.yaml and remove the known_legacy/descriptor fallback path.

excerpt: # map profile declares |y| <= 8 m as its acceptance envelope; obstacle ⏎ distance is retained as descriptive guidance evidence and is not a gate.
claim: The cross-track acceptance envelope has three disagreeing owners and no enforcer: map_profiles.yaml declares benchmark.max_cross_track_m (long_open_featured_speed 0.5, core_60 0.5, core_60_pv 0.75) and describes it as bounding the avoidance envelope; runner overrides it with hard-coded constants (long_open_featured_speed 8.0, core_60/_pv 0.75 via _acceptance_threshold_for_profile without the registry entry) and its comments claim "the hard out-of-map gate"/"benchmark corridor checks" enforce it independently; report.py computes cross_track_error_p95_m but explicitly never gates it and no corridor/out-of-map check exists anywhere in the judge.
failure_scenario: A long_open_featured_speed run deviating 7 m from its 0.5 m declared LIO-calibration corridor (or any out-of-map excursion) PASSes; REPORT.html shows a limit (8.0/0.75) that contradicts the registry; readers of the runner/registry comments believe an envelope gate exists.
direction: Decide one owner (registry) and either implement the corridor gate in report.py from the descriptor or delete the per-profile limits and the misleading comments.

claim: Two mission files share mission id external_mode_pillar_route but have different geometry (pillar_detour/mission_finish at x=-6.0 vs -5.5).
failure_scenario: Evidence, reports and mission_id-keyed comparisons across runs cannot distinguish which geometry was flown; a regression comparison between structured_obstacle (pillar.yaml) and the scenario default (external_mode_pillar.yaml) silently mixes routes.
direction: Make mission id unique per file and validate uniqueness in the registry loader.

claim: Freshness bounds for the same streams disagree between product consumers and the judge: /lio/odometry_propagated is stale after 0.20 s in the adapter, 0.5 s in navigation_runtime and 0.50 s in the judge stream table (0.10 s pre-activation in the scenario); external odometry is stale after 0.20 s in the judge but 0.5 s in the bridge.
failure_scenario: The judge stream-freshness gate can report PASS for a propagated-odometry gap (0.2-0.5 s) that the adapter treats as stale (hold/handover), and can FAIL external odometry gaps the bridge accepts; judge evidence does not reflect the product contract.
direction: Single declared freshness contract per stream consumed by both product YAML generation and judge thresholds (generate one from the other, or cross-check at runner startup).

claim: Guard is implemented with bare assert statements, which are stripped under python -O / PYTHONOPTIMIZE; reproduced: with a forced-missing marker the guard exits 1 normally but prints PASS and exits 0 under -O (OUT/guard_O_test.py).
failure_scenario: A CI/Make environment with PYTHONOPTIMIZE set silently disables the state-transport-trace scope guard (false PASS).
direction: Replace assert with explicit checks + sys.exit(1) like the other guards.

excerpt: for p in (ROOT / "src").rglob("*.yaml") ⏎ if "test" not in p.parts
claim: "no production YAML enable" only scans src/**.yaml; the production runtime parameter files actually loaded by navigation_runtime_node live in config/runtime/*.yaml and are not scanned.
failure_scenario: Adding navigation_runtime.inject_exact_optimization_failed_once: true to config/runtime/mapping.yaml passes the guard although the SITL-only fault injector would then be enabled by default in every run.
direction: Scan config/ as well (or derive the list of product YAMLs from runner/launch).

excerpt: if "NavigationCommand, " in gate and "create_publisher(\n            NavigationCommand" in gate:
claim: The "test gate must never publish NavigationCommand" ban matches only one exact line-break + 12-space formatting; self.create_publisher(NavigationCommand, topic, qos) on one line (standard rclpy style) passes. Lines 66/68 required markers are equally whitespace-exact.
failure_scenario: A future edit adding a single-line NavigationCommand publisher to world_observation_gate.py passes CI; a reformat (black/ruff) of the existing code makes the guard FAIL spuriously.
direction: Use ast parsing of Python sources (find create_publisher calls and their first arg) instead of formatted substrings.

claim: Product YAML declares tracking_experiment.mode "off" ("Explicit off keeps the normal tracking and health responses active") but every runner path (CLI default, _tracking_experiment_payload() default) overwrites it with "relaxed", which suppresses tracking-triggered MAIN emergency, PX4 anchor rejects and FAST-LIO health rejects (runner.py:644-673). The YAML value is never the effective default.
failure_scenario: A default make run / make run-gui PASS is produced with six safety responses suppressed (qualification_eligible=false in metadata but verdict still PASS); anyone reading the YAML believes gates are active.
direction: Make the YAML the single default (runner passes mode only when explicitly requested) or change YAML to relaxed and state it; surface qualification_eligible=false in the top-level verdict.

claim: V7: runner re-derives the mission waypoint default behavior with a constant "stop", while the C++ loader defaults a waypoint without behavior to pass_through unless hold_s>0 or it is the last waypoint.
failure_scenario: A mission whose first waypoint omits behavior and hold_s is pass_through in C++ (controller skips it inside the acceptance ball) but the harness sets allow_initial_pass_through_skip=False and flags the legitimate prefix skip as an ordering failure.
direction: Expose the resolved mission (behaviors) from the C++ loader (e.g. a validator CLI emitting JSON) and consume it in the harness instead of re-parsing YAML.

claim: pillar_waypoint_index and pillar geometry are a hard-coded per-profile table with default 3; profiles not listed (occlusion_featured, occlusion_degenerate, tunnel_*, forest_clutter, structured_obstacle) get index 3 and the template pillar_center_enu [-4.5,2.5,3.0] from external_mode_scenario.yaml even though those worlds have no pillar there; the canonical registry name occlusion_featured gets 3 while its alias occlusion gets 2 and a different center.
failure_scenario: For tunnel/forest/occlusion_degenerate the single-pillar planned-clearance assertion (external_mode_scenario.py:3099-3110) runs against a non-existent obstacle (vacuous PASS or spurious FAIL depending on route); occlusion vs occlusion_featured evaluate different waypoints for the same world.
direction: Declare route obstacle / checked waypoint in map_profiles.yaml (route_obstacles already exists) and derive the check from SDF geometry; remove the table.

claim: _write_runtime does a non-atomic read-modify-write of runtime.json and on any parse error silently resets to {} before writing; the SIGTERM/SIGINT guard raises KeyboardInterrupt asynchronously, which can land inside write_text and truncate the file.
failure_scenario: A signal during a write truncates runtime.json; the finally-branch _stop_and_report then rewrites it from {} and drops failures/startup fields, so report.build sees failures=[] and missing provenance (wrong evidence; possible verdict change).
direction: Write via temp file + os.replace (as _finalize_nominal_snapshot_capture already does) and fail loudly on unparsable runtime.json.

claim: p50/p95/p99 have 10 separate implementations with two different definitions: 8 copies (evaluation, monitor, html_report, external_mode_scenario, analyze_runtime_evidence, analyze_e5, benchmark_evidence_writer, state_transport_analysis) use nearest-index with Python round() (banker's rounding, no NaN filtering) and 2 copies use linear interpolation with finite filtering. Reproduced (OUT/pct_repro.py): 10x0.1 + one 5.0 gives p95=5.0 (nearest) vs 2.55 (linear); n=2 p50 picks the lower element but n=4 p50 the upper; a NaN in the input silently changes the order statistic.
failure_scenario: The same "p95" gate (e.g. max_cross_track_p95_m, latency p95) gives different verdicts depending on which tool computed it, and the result flips by one full sample when (n-1)*p lands on .5 depending on parity.
direction: One shared statistics module (explicit definition, finite filtering, documented tie rule) imported by all tools.

claim: _bracket re-sorts the whole measured stream on every call and is called once per reference sample (tracking) and twice per estimate sample (evaluate_localization then _ate_rpe) -> O(N*M log M). Measured on a copy (OUT/perf_bracket.py): 3000 samples/stream = 4.1 s for evaluate_localization; a 5-minute 50 Hz run (15k samples) extrapolates to ~100 s for localization alone plus the two tracking pairs.
failure_scenario: report.build after long missions (navigation_generalization 395 m) takes minutes, extending the post-flight window and risking harness timeouts; cost grows quadratically with mission length.
direction: Sort each stream once and pass the sorted stamps (bisect) into _bracket; reuse brackets between evaluate_localization and _ate_rpe.

claim: Localization ATE/RPE subtracts LIO position (lio_odom frame) from Gazebo truth (world frame) without the T_L_G frame witness that evaluate_tracking applies; RPE uses consecutive matched samples (~20-100 ms apart) instead of a distance/time window.
failure_scenario: ATE carries the constant spawn/initialization offset (base_link spawn z=0.2 in world vs lio_odom origin) and any initial yaw misalignment; RPE is dominated by sample noise, so both reported localization-quality numbers are wrong evidence for LIO drift.
direction: Apply the same _frame_witness transform as tracking and compute RPE over a declared delta (e.g. 1 m / 1 s).

excerpt: for command in reference: ⏎ bracket = _bracket(measured, int(command["source_stamp_ns"]), max_gap_s)
claim: evaluation_window restricts only the coverage computation; the tracking error statistics (p95/max used by the acceptance policy) are computed over every reference sample, including samples outside the window.
failure_scenario: Errors during excluded intervals (e.g. activation/handover or terminal hold outside the declared window) enter p95/max and can FAIL (or dilute) the tracking dimension that the window was meant to scope.
direction: Filter reference samples by the evaluation window before _tracking_pair and report the excluded count.

claim: V7 inventory: the lifecycle reducer and the C0_SW safety-stop witness re-derive C++ ownership semantics from raw ordinals: bundle_source {2,3} = CandidateSource::kRetained/kEmergency (candidate_bundle.hpp:27-32), purpose 0/2 = RetainedValidationPurpose::kAfterFailedReplacement/kTerminalMainMonitor (navigation_runtime_node.hpp:316-320), planner_status 4 = PlannerStatus::kFailed (planner_status.hpp:9-17), planner_disposition 4 = PlannerResultDisposition::RetainCommittedCommand (planner_fsm.hpp:215-222), retained disposition_code 2/3/4/5/8.
failure_scenario: Inserting or reordering an enumerator in any of those C++ enums silently changes which transactions the judge treats as emergency/terminal-monitor/fail-closed witnesses; C0_SW product_logic PASS for PAUSED_SAFETY_STOP then depends on stale ordinals.
direction: Emit enum names (or a generated Python enum module from the C++ headers) in the evidence and compare by name.

excerpt: for obstacle in self.config.get("collision_obstacles", []): ⏎ ... ⏎ obstacle_clearance = signed_distance - vehicle_radius
claim: Collision/clearance truth is evaluated only at discrete ground-truth sample points (OdometryPublisher rate, ~50 Hz) with no swept-segment check between consecutive samples; the minimum clearance between samples can be lower than any sampled value by up to v*dt/2 (0.08 m at 8 m/s, 0.05 m at 5 m/s).
failure_scenario: At the 5-8 m/s speed profiles a pass that dips below minimum_collision_clearance_m=0.10 (or grazes a thin beam) between two samples is reported as clearing it -> false PASS of the clearance gate.
direction: Compute segment-to-obstacle distance between consecutive truth samples (closed form for box/cylinder vs segment) or bound the error with v*dt and subtract it.

excerpt: if self.execution == "mission": ⏎ ... ⏎ if self.collision_count > 0: ⏎ failures.append("ground-truth vehicle collision envelope was breached")
claim: All ground-truth safety gates in the scenario verdict (collision envelope, configured clearance margin, 0.05 m pillar margin, speed contract, stable takeoff, terminal outcome) are nested under execution == "mission"; the single_goal execution path never adds them to failures even though collision_count is computed.
failure_scenario: An adapter regression run with execution: single_goal that collides returns exit 0 / outcome ABORTED_OPERATOR without a collision failure from the scenario (only evaluation.py safety dimension would notice).
direction: Apply the geometry/safety gates independent of execution kind.

claim: The harness selects the first EXTERNALn bit set in can_set_nav_states_mask as "the" navigation mode instead of matching the registered component (name/arming-check id).
failure_scenario: With any other external mode registered (BUILD_PX4_ROS2_EXAMPLES=1 examples, a stale component) the harness arms and activates the wrong mode; evidence then attributes that mode's behavior to the navigation stack.
direction: Match the mode by the registration name/ID emitted by the adapter (EXTERNAL_MODE_READY marker can include it).

excerpt: def stop(_signum: int, _frame: Any) -> None: ⏎ ... ⏎ scenario.finish(scenario.terminal_outcome or "INTERRUPTED")
claim: SIGINT/SIGTERM handler runs finish() (writes scenario.json, closes the evidence writer) asynchronously in the middle of whatever rclpy callback was executing; the interrupted callback then resumes and may _record into a closed writer or mutate state after the summary was written.
failure_scenario: A runner timeout/stop during a busy callback yields a scenario.json whose counters disagree with scenario.jsonl, or an exception after finish that loses the terminal marker -> NOT_EVALUABLE / writer-integrity failures.
direction: Set a flag in the handler and call finish() from the spin loop.

claim: For expected fail_closed profiles the scenario contract accepts either a ModeCompleted failure or a terminal safety pause as the valid negative outcome (_fail_closed_contract_failures), and the tick loop finishes with FAILED_COMPONENT when ModeStatus is FAILED; report._sim_report maps FAILED_COMPONENT to FAIL unconditionally and only PAUSED_SAFETY_STOP can PASS a fail-closed profile.
failure_scenario: no_path / occlusion_degenerate / tunnel_smooth that fail closed via ModeStatus FAILED (a correct fail-closed behavior per the scenario) are reported FAIL; the two verdict owners disagree on what a correct negative result is.
direction: Define the negative-outcome contract once (enum of accepted terminal outcomes per expected_outcome) and use it in both scenario and report.

excerpt: threshold_ns = int(self.stale_after_s * 1e9) ⏎ if threshold_ns > 0 and gap_ns > threshold_ns:
claim: Clock-domain mixing: stream stale/gap events are computed from wall-clock arrival time (time.time_ns(), non-monotonic) against stale_after_s budgets that common.yaml documents as the product freshness budgets (defined on ROS/sim time); a monotonic arrival stamp is recorded but not used for these statistics.
failure_scenario: With Gazebo real-time factor < 1 (GUI/CPU load) a stream that is fresh in sim time exceeds its wall budget -> false freshness FAIL; with RTF > 1 real sim-time staleness is hidden; an NTP step during a run creates spurious or negative gaps.
direction: Evaluate freshness in the source clock (sim-time stamps vs /clock) and use monotonic time only for executor-stall diagnostics.

excerpt: mission_condition = None if not outcome else outcome in {"PAUSED_SAFETY_STOP", "FAILED_COMPONENT"} ⏎ None if cross_p95 is None or cross_limit is None else cross_p95 <= cross_limit
claim: REPORT.html computes its own "overall" verdict with rules that contradict report.json: it gates cross-track p95 <= max_cross_track_p95_m (report.py explicitly does not) and accepts FAILED_COMPONENT as a valid fail-closed mission outcome (report.py maps it to FAIL). Three verdict owners (scenario exit code, report.verdict, renderer overall) plus evaluation.assessment_status.
failure_scenario: The same session shows FAIL in report.json but PASS in REPORT.html (fail-closed via ModeStatus FAILED), or PASS in report.json and FAIL in REPORT.html (detour exceeding the hard-coded cross-track limit); reviewers act on whichever artifact they open.
direction: Renderer must display report.json verdict/reasons only; move any additional gate into report.py.

claim: The MID-360 scan grid (720x28, azimuth -pi..pi, elevation -7..52 deg, range 40 m) that the visibility bridge uses to reconstruct free-space ray directions is hard-coded in three places (lidar model SDF, runner CLI params, bridge defaults); makeVisibilityCloud only validates width/height counts, not the angles, against the actual sensor.
failure_scenario: Changing the sensor FOV in model.sdf without the runner produces free-space endpoints along wrong elevations; ROG-Map raycasting then marks voxels KNOWN_FREE along rays that never existed (possibly through obstacles), feeding BACKUP KNOWN_FREE certification with fabricated evidence in SITL.
direction: Read the grid from the SDF (runner already parses it for the range overlay) and pass it through, or have the bridge read the gz LaserScan metadata; add a test comparing the three.

claim: A local dataset manifest (dataset.yaml with config.path) declares its own estimator config (extrinsic, point-time encoding, ranges) and data.py validates that file exists, but run_dataset always generates fast_lio params and the lidar->imu TF from config/runtime/dataset.yaml (AIST MID-360 values); context["config"] is never consumed.
failure_scenario: A local Mid-360 capture with a different IMU-LiDAR extrinsic or timestamp encoding is replayed with the AIST extrinsic (translation [-0.019391,-0.000278,0.080926]) and reported as a normal dataset-check PASS/FAIL, i.e. wrong estimator evidence.
direction: Use context["config"] as the fast_lio parameter source (or reject manifests whose config differs from dataset.yaml).

excerpt: AbsoluteDeadline(const double start_time, const double budget_seconds) ⏎ AbsoluteDeadline(const double simulation_deadline, ⏎ const std::int64_t steady_deadline_ns)
claim: Two constructors differ only in the type of the 2nd argument (double seconds budget vs int64 absolute steady ns) and in the meaning of the 1st argument (start time vs absolute deadline). Any integer-typed second argument (e.g. an int budget, a size_t or an int64 ms value) silently binds to the absolute-ns overload.
failure_scenario: A caller writing AbsoluteDeadline(now, 1) or passing an integer millisecond budget gets a steady deadline 1 ns after the steady epoch -> immediately expired -> every stage reports PLANNER_SOLVE_TIMEOUT.
direction: Replace the overload pair with named factories (fromBudget(start_s, budget_s) / fromRequest(sim_deadline_s, SteadyNs)) using strong types.

excerpt: inline navigation_world_model::UnknownPolicy candidateCertificatePolicy( ⏎ const CandidateCommandBundle& candidate, ⏎ const navigation_world_model::UnknownPolicy mission_policy) { ⏎ (void)candidate; ⏎ return mission_policy;
claim: candidateCertificatePolicy ignores the candidate and returns the mission policy; it is called at planner.cpp:789/1662/2717 and planner_facade.cpp:450 while the export world_validator closure (planner.cpp:1135-1152) calls unknownPolicy() directly. The indirection suggests role/candidate-specific policy that does not exist; readers cannot tell which call sites are authoritative.
failure_scenario: If someone later adds candidate-specific logic here, the export-time world_validator closure (which bypasses it) will recertify with a different MAIN policy than admission used -> admission/recertification divergence.
direction: Delete the helper or route every certification (including the export closure) through one policy function.

claim: Validator requires the role partition to be contiguous with EXACT float equality, while CmdTraj::commitCandidate (cmd_traj.h:390-405) accepts the same partition with 1e-6 s tolerance. Two acceptance rules for the same role schedule.
failure_scenario: A role schedule produced by arithmetic (e.g. shifted/clipped inherited backup interval) that differs by 1 ulp passes commitCandidate/warm-start but fails validateExecutableCandidate with kInvalidRoleSchedule (or vice versa) -> spurious rejection of a certified candidate.
direction: Define the role partition on integer ns (or one shared tolerance) in a single validator used by builder, validator and commit.

excerpt: navigation_planning::PlanningStartMode::kMeasuredEmergencyBrake ⏎ ... ⏎ return commitEmergencyBrake( ⏎ measured, request.start_state.yaw_rad, 0.0, ⏎ planner_context_->getSimTime(), std::nullopt,
claim: The typed measured-emergency branch of plan() has no producer (grep: runtime calls planner_->commitEmergencyBrake directly at navigation_runtime_node.cpp:8143; no code builds kMeasuredEmergencyBrake). The branch also hard-codes yaw_rate 0 (KinematicState has no yaw-rate field) and starts the brake at getSimTime() rather than the measured source_stamp_ns, with no latency compensation.
failure_scenario: If this branch is ever enabled, a yawing vehicle gets an emergency yaw polynomial with zero initial yaw rate (commanded yaw-rate step at handover) and a start state that is stale by the request latency.
direction: Remove the dead branch or give KinematicState a yaw rate and a start-stamp->start_WT rule, with a test.

claim: time_consuming_ is written by solves under replan_lock_; moduleTimeConsumingSnapshot reads it under replan_lock_, but getModuleTimeConsuming reads AND zeroes it without any lock (and getLatestReplanLog 749-753 copies it unlocked). Mixed locking discipline for one vector.
failure_scenario: A diagnostics caller of getModuleTimeConsuming concurrent with a solve races on the vector elements (UB); counters may be zeroed mid-solve so stage timing evidence is wrong.
direction: Protect time_consuming_ with one lock in all accessors or make the diagnostic a per-solve value returned in PlanningOutcome.

claim: A compile-time-constant false flag keeps dead branches alive: connected_goal term (4025), acceptance-fillet cap (4170-4185), corner branch guard (4210). Also the log at 4123 prints a hard-coded 'local=20.000' instead of the PlanningTimingContract::kLocalWindowM value actually passed at 4112.
failure_scenario: Readers/reviewers reason about fillet behaviour that can never execute; if kLocalWindowM changes, the rejection log reports a wrong support value.
direction: Delete the dead flag/branches and format the actual constant in the log.

excerpt: Polytope candidate_sfc; ⏎ bool candidate_aligned_sfc = false; ⏎ ... ⏎ braking_seed_inside_sfc = ⏎ candidate_sfc.PointIsInside(braking_control_points.col(i));
claim: The first hull-containment test is evaluated against a default-constructed Polytope; Polytope::PointIsInside returns false when undefined/validPlanes fails (polytope.cpp:155-158, validPlanes requires rows>0). The test therefore always fails, always records kVisibilityHull as last_reject_stage and visibility_hull_pass_count stays 0; only the aligned-SFC path can succeed.
failure_scenario: Backup diagnostics (last_reject_stage, visibility_hull_pass_count) consumed by classifyPlannerFailure/judge report a visibility-hull rejection on every switch candidate, masking the real rejection stage; wasted Bezier evaluation per candidate.
direction: Delete the dead visibility-hull test and its counters, or build the visibility SFC it was meant to use.

excerpt: const auto sample_count = static_cast<std::size_t>(std::ceil( ⏎ duration_s / sample_dt_s)); ⏎ if (sample_count > 10000000U) return false;
claim: backupEntersAcceptanceAndEndsOutside detects entry into the pass-through acceptance ball by point sampling at sample_traj_dt_s (a chord through the ball shorter than v*dt is missed) and returns false (='does not cross', i.e. accept) when the sample count exceeds 1e7. Both degrade toward acceptance.
failure_scenario: A braking suffix that grazes the acceptance sphere between two samples and stops outside is accepted as a legal disposition; the route-regression certificate later rejects the correction back to that waypoint -> mission stall at a pass-through waypoint.
direction: Use the analytic first-visit helper (firstAcceptanceSphereVisit) already used for MAIN, and fail closed on the size guard.

claim: The 'steady-state' fast path assumes contiguous scans (scan.start == previous scan.end). In simultaneous_scan mode (the sim configuration) RosLidarAdapter sets start_time==end_time==header stamp (ros_lidar_adapter.cpp:135,263-267), so propagation_start (previous stamp) never equals scan.start and every scan takes the merge path: validate the whole 1 s prior_imu_history_ and allocate/merge it with the group, contrary to the comment.
failure_scenario: Sim at 10 Hz scans with 200-1000 Hz IMU: each scan validates and copies 200-1000 retained samples plus the group on the estimator thread; wasted work grows with IMU rate.
direction: Define steady state as start_time == group.propagation_start_time (the synchronizer-provided epoch) and keep the history merge only for prior/rebase epochs; add a sim-mode test asserting the fast path.

claim: Every IKFoM iteration (up to registration.maximum_iterations=4) repeats the full k-NN search and plane fit for all filtered points; data.converge is ignored. Upstream FAST-LIO re-associates only when the previous iterate converged, so this path does up to 4x the nearest-search work per scan.
failure_scenario: Degenerate/slow-converging scans use all 4 iterations -> 4 full searches of the ikd-tree while an asynchronous rebuild may hold subtree locks (Search waits on search_mutex_counter), stretching the worst-case scan time exactly when registration is already struggling.
direction: Make re-association policy explicit (associate on first iteration and after convergence, or every iteration by design) and record the choice with a timing test; reuse neighbor sets between iterations when the increment is small.

claim: The typed health contract exports the raw ordinal of the C++ LidarUpdateFailureClass enum; there is no message-level constant set, so any reordering/insertion in estimator_diagnostics.hpp silently changes the meaning of reason_code for the adapter/judge (same pattern as R-05 on the judge side).

claim: Static guards are substring presence tests on formatted source (exact indentation, first occurrence); a marker inside a comment or dead code satisfies them and a harmless reformat breaks them (same pattern in check_mission_authority_cut.py:44-62, check_execution_authority_cut.py:26-44).
failure_scenario: Guard PASS does not prove the call is live (a commented-out call still matches); reformatting runner.py fails CI without a behavior change.
direction: Move to AST/libclang-level checks or unit tests asserting behavior; at minimum strip comments before matching.

claim: CI runs only tools/runtime/tests; tools/tests (test_build.py, test_data.py) run only via make test; check_qualification_evidence_scope.py and check_software_qualification_scope.py are never run in CI. The permanent guard list is also duplicated between ci.yml and pre_main_gate.static_guard_names() (no single source), and pre_main_gate likewise omits tools/tests.
failure_scenario: Regressions in tools/data.py / build.py or scope violations are not caught on PRs.
direction: Add tools/tests discovery to CI; document or delete the branch-only scope guards.

claim: The .msg field parser silently drops any line not exactly two tokens: constants written with spaces (uint8 X = 1) or fields with default values are invisible.
failure_scenario: A reformatted .msg (ROS allows "uint8 ROLE_MAIN = 0") makes required constants appear missing (spurious FAIL) and a new defaulted field escapes the allowlist (false PASS).
direction: Use rosidl_adapter parser or a regex that handles constants/defaults.

claim: Expected outcome has two sources: a hard-coded profile set (3252) and the registry expected_outcome (3407, with vocabulary translation mission_complete->complete). The registry value later overwrites the first; the mission_timeout_s min(60) side effect stays keyed to the hard-coded set.
failure_scenario: Adding a new fail_closed profile in the registry yields expected_outcome=fail_closed but keeps the 120-300 s timeout, and renaming a profile silently diverges the two lists.
direction: Derive both outcome and timeout policy from the registry entry only; use one outcome vocabulary.

claim: Run metadata hard-codes planner/command timing values that are owned by planner.yaml (replan_forward_dt_s, solve_deadline_s) and the typed C++ PlanningTimingContract::kPlannerRateHz instead of reading them.
failure_scenario: Changing planner.yaml or the typed contract leaves every metadata.json reporting the old timing contract -> wrong provenance evidence used by reports/analysis.
direction: Read from the generated planner.yaml / a RUNTIME_CONFIG_EFFECTIVE timing witness like dynamics.

claim: Config layering for judge/runner runtime settings is a shallow merge: a runtime_overrides.thresholds or .streams block would replace the entire common.yaml sub-map instead of overriding one key; any runtime: block inside the workflow YAML is silently discarded.
failure_scenario: A workflow YAML adding runtime_overrides: {streams: {imu: {...}}} drops all other stream definitions, disabling their freshness checks without error.
direction: Deep-merge with explicit key validation (reject unknown keys).

excerpt: if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("waypoint_accepted", True) ⏎ item.get("waypoint_accepted") is True
claim: Two waypoint-acceptance reducers in the same module disagree on a missing waypoint_accepted field: evaluate_session treats it as accepted, evaluate_software_qualification as not accepted.
failure_scenario: An acceptance event lacking the flag makes the C0_IFP mission dimension PASS while the C0_SW product-logic axis reports NOT_EVALUABLE for the same run.
direction: Parse waypoint acceptance once (typed) and share the result.

excerpt: safety_radius = sum(value for value in safety_components if value is not None)
claim: Python-version sensitivity: sum() of floats uses Neumaier compensation from 3.12; the canonical interpreter is pinned by path (/usr/bin/python3) not version. Reproduced: test_html_report.test_spatial_envelopes_are_loaded_from_session_parameters passes on 3.12/3.13 and fails on 3.10/3.11 (0.8700000000000001 != 0.87).
failure_scenario: On a host whose /usr/bin/python3 is 3.10/3.11 (Ubuntu 22.04) the evaluator/test results differ at ULP level and exact-equality checks flip.
direction: Pin the minimum Python version in require_canonical_python and avoid exact float equality (math.isclose / fsum).

claim: The C0_IFP assessment_status PASS branch is unreachable: motion_status is always NOT_EVALUABLE, so assessment_status is FAIL or NOT_EVALUABLE for every run.
failure_scenario: Consumers that key on evaluation.assessment_status == PASS never see it; the effective verdict lives elsewhere (report.py), making two verdict owners.
direction: Make the unreachable state explicit (drop PASS from the enum until W9) or move the motion dimension out of the conjunction.

claim: V7: the harness hard-codes NavigationModeStatus state/reason ordinals (mirrors NavigationModeStatus.msg:13-24) although it imports the message class, and re-implements the localization-divergence thresholds (0.45/0.5 m, 0.75/1.0 m/s, 0.5 s) that mirror the product watchdog.
failure_scenario: A msg constant renumbering or a product watchdog change leaves the harness verdict and report names stale without any test failing.
direction: Use NavigationModeStatus constants; read watchdog limits from the product parameter file.

excerpt: handover_reason = "mission did not reach COMPLETE outcome: PAUSED_SAFETY_STOP" ⏎ reasons = [reason for reason in reasons if reason != handover_reason]
claim: The fail-closed PASS path removes a reason by exact string equality with text produced in _mission_acceptance (f"mission did not reach COMPLETE outcome: {outcome}").
failure_scenario: Any rewording of the _mission_acceptance message (or a different outcome spelling) silently turns every valid fail-closed PAUSED_SAFETY_STOP run into FAIL.
direction: Carry typed reason codes (enum) and filter by code.

claim: Per-message bounded-history maintenance copies/shifts whole lists (4096-element delete-from-front and a 512-element slice copy on every sample) inside the single-threaded monitor spin.
failure_scenario: At 200 Hz IMU plus the other streams the monitor spends O(5k) element moves per message; under GUI load the monitor lags, and because stale/gap events use arrival time at the monitor (R7-39) the lag itself becomes false stale evidence.
direction: Use collections.deque(maxlen=...) for both histories.

claim: The characterization reference clamps u to [0,1] but evaluates the quintic jerk polynomial at the clamp: after the last segment (held at local_elapsed=duration) the harness keeps sending jerk = 60*d/T^3 (non-zero) with zero velocity/acceleration in TrajectorySetpoint.jerk and in the recorded reference_jerk_ned.
failure_scenario: Post-segment hold samples carry a constant non-zero jerk feed-forward/reference, contaminating jerk statistics of the closed-loop characterization report.
direction: Return zero derivatives outside the open interval (u<=0 before start, u>=1 after end).

claim: _group_exists scans every /proc/<pid>/stat on each call; runner._wait_until calls it for every registered role every 0.25 s and Session.stop polls it every 50 ms per group.
failure_scenario: On a developer host with a few hundred processes, readiness polling reads thousands of proc files per second in the orchestrator; shutdown of ~15 groups adds seconds of CPU; not safety-relevant.
direction: Check membership once per poll (single /proc scan mapping pgid->states) or use os.waitpid/pidfd for owned children.

claim: Scenario keys have multiple in-code defaults that disagree with each other and with the YAML: pillar_waypoint_index defaults to 3 in _ground_truth and 1 in finish(); wall_timeout_s 120 (code) vs 360 (yaml); takeoff_timeout_s 45 (code, runner manual path) vs 220 (yaml); mission_timeout_s 90 (scenario) vs 120 (runner fallback) vs yaml 120.
failure_scenario: A scenario config lacking pillar_waypoint_index measures the 2-D pillar clearance at index 3 but asserts the planned-detour clearance at index 1; any consumer launching the scenario with a partial config gets different timeouts than the runner-generated one.
direction: Single typed scenario-config schema with one default per key (dataclass loaded once, unknown/missing keys rejected).
